finalExcerpt:
`parse_price("1,234.50")` now returns `1234.5`, and all 5 tests pass. That includes the existing ones and the new regression test.

The fix is in `parse_price` in `inventory.py`. It now treats commas as thousands separators when they match the rule in `ISSUE.md`: one to three digits, then comma-plus
…
0"`, `"$3"` and `"12,50"` behave as before. I didn't touch `total_value`.

I added `test_thousands_separator` to `tests/test_inventory.py`. It covers `"1,234.50"` and `"$1,234,567"`.

Two things to know:
- A bare `"1,234"` is still read as a European decimal, so it gives `1.234`. The issue only defines a thousands separator when a dot or another comma group follows, so I left that case alone.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` fails with an import error in this repo, because `tests/` has no `__init__.py`. I ran the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` instead.
